CLOSED — landed as bb1478169758703f236e6b26b8e5c908d94dad5f (Gerrit change 1640, MERGED 2026-08-12T08:53:56Z), LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 on patch set 2 (CI run 31577972486 SUCCESS). All 8 ACs verified green against the LANDED code, not just the local branch (19/19 tests, plus each AC's recorded verify command run individually). Closed --class preexisting: git -S shows the dead 401 check predates the 2026-07-22 adapters/jira relocation and never functioned, so it is a long-standing latent defect, not a regression.

CI history for the record: two Verified -1s on patch set 1, both triaged as unrelated test-scaffolding races and NOT rechecked blindly a third time. Run 31571454820 (macos py3.13, 1 failed / 12134 passed) failed test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev_heldout on a stray .git/objects/maintenance.lock — the test byte-compares the whole tracker dir including .git/. Run 31575183167 (ubuntu py3.12, 1 failed / 152 passed) failed test_plan_review_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union at a FIXTURE PRECONDITION ('clones do not share a base') — clone B had not synced clone A's push, so the append-only property under test was never exercised. Different tests, different platforms, neither on this change's code path. Resolved by rebasing onto fresh origin/main (6 commits behind) and pushing patch set 2, which went green first try. Both flakes documented on chewed-illicit-blacklemur.

*** OPERATOR ACTION STILL REQUIRED — THIS FIX DOES NOT RESTORE THE BRIDGE ***
The JIRA_API_TOKEN secret is genuinely expired/revoked: all six Mode 1 runs failed on the FIRST ACLI call while the workflow's own 'acli jira auth login' step succeeded, i.e. the token is rejected at first use. This change makes that failure legible in one line — a distinct typed error, no wasted retries, exit 2 instead of 1, and a message naming the secret to rotate — but the scheduled Reconcile Bridge will KEEP FAILING Mode 1 until someone rotates JIRA_API_TOKEN. Rotation needs a new secret value and is deliberately outside what this ticket could deliver: re-running 'acli auth login' with the same rejected token cannot help, and inventing a refresh flow or storing credentials somewhere new was explicitly out of scope.

Follow-on work, all linked discovered_from this ticket:
- subzero-locustal-junebug — git delivery fails on TLS 'server certificate verification failed' (2 runs, converged passes whose events never reached origin/tickets)
- freeborn-dizzy-raven — rejected ref pushes: stale --force-with-lease on refs/reconciler/last-pass, lost race on refs/heads/tickets (2 runs)
- callous-wavy-kite — continuous-loop re-dispatch HTTP 422 on a disabled workflow (2 runs whose reconcile SUCCEEDED; arguably should be a benign no-op, not a red run)
- satisfied-emerald-grayling — ACLI 'command cancelled' emitted and SWALLOWED in the outbound link-apply loop, with the enclosing batch_outcome recorded as success (the silent-divergence class); strong lead is the missing --yes on workitem link create/delete
- chewed-illicit-blacklemur — the two CI test-scaffolding flakes above

Also noted but NOT fixed here (scope discipline): dispatch_one.py has a best-effort 'except Exception' around link ops that would swallow an AcliAuthError raised mid-link-apply as non-fatal. Not a regression — the old CalledProcessError was swallowed there too, and worse, counted as links_applied — and unreachable for the observed failures, which all abort on the first search call.
